key_insight: A small set of modules — and the interactions between them — explain most of the performance differences in the PSO-X framework; quantifying these contributions lets you focus configuration effort where it matters most.
problem_solved: Modular PSO frameworks contain many interchangeable components and interaction degrees of freedom, making automated configuration costly and opaque; this work identifies which modules and interactions actually drive performance.
method: Systematic evaluation of PSO-X by sampling/configuring many module combinations across a suite of continuous optimization benchmarks.
Statistical effect quantification (variance decomposition / factorial analysis / importance scores) to separate main effects from pairwise and higher-order interactions.
Sensitivity and ranking analysis to produce a prioritized list of influential modules and interaction patterns useful for pruning the configuration space.
impact: Enables practitioners and AutoML systems to reduce search complexity, speed up algorithm selection/tuning, and increase interpretability by concentrating on the few modules and interactions that matter most.
visual_elements: Stacked bar chart showing fraction of performance variance explained by main effects vs. interactions vs. residual noise.
Heatmap of pairwise interaction strengths between modules (darker = stronger interaction effect).
Ranked list or horizontal bar chart of top N most influential modules with short icons (e.g., topology, inertia, update rule).
Pipeline diagram illustrating how module choices feed into PSO-X and lead to performance outcomes (for quick conceptual overview).
paper_title: Quantifying the Impact of Modules and Their Interactions in the PSO-X Framework
paper_authors: Christian L. Camacho-Villalón, Ana Nikolikj, Katharina Dost, Eva Tuba, Sašo Džeroski
